capability.summary: Evaluates constant-velocity and quintic smooth-step prescribed trajectories, validates analytical speed/acceleration ceilings, and checks a separately supplied achieved state against a requested sample.
inputs: absolute logical time (s) or fixed-step index and timestep
total step count for fixed-step evaluation
achieved rigid-body snapshot and commit tolerances

model.name: Constant-velocity and quintic smooth-step prescribed motion
model.formulation: Evaluates the declared trajectory at absolute logical time or a fixed logical step. The quintic smooth-step profile has zero endpoint velocity and acceleration; constant-velocity mode has endpoint velocity discontinuities.
equations: Quintic smooth-step position profile: s(u)=10u^3−15u^4+6u^5, for normalized u in [0,1].
Trajectory position is interpolated between declared endpoints using the selected profile.
assumptions: Motion is prescribed by a trajectory definition rather than derived from applied forces.
The caller owns actual body advancement and supplies the achieved state for commit validation.
Fixed-step evaluation uses caller-declared timestep and total step count.
model.timeModel: Supports absolute logical-time evaluation and deterministic fixed-step indexing; no clock or scheduler is owned by the provider.
validity: Declared peak speed and acceleration ceilings are analytically validated by the underlying definition.
Achieved-state tolerances are supplied by the caller.

hostResponsibilities: Choose logical time or fixed-step schedule.
Apply the requested state to the host body.
Supply achieved state for commit validation.
Own collisions, forces, and physical response.
Resolve the typed provider interface from the loaded bundle instance.

validation: Adapter delegates absolute-time and fixed-step evaluation to PrescribedKinematicMotion.
Adapter delegates achieved-state commit validation to PrescribedKinematicMotion.
Underlying model validates analytical peak speed and acceleration ceilings.
knownGaps: This is kinematic prescription, not a force-driven dynamics solver.
Constant-velocity mode has endpoint velocity discontinuities by design.

learningObjectives: Distinguish prescribed kinematics from force-driven dynamics.
Compare constant-velocity and quintic smooth-step boundary behavior.
